**Issue Identified**: The StatefulSet `app` in namespace `default` was unable to start because its VolumeClaimTemplate specified a non-existent StorageClass `fast-ssd`. Kubernetes couldn't provision persistent volumes, leaving PVCs `data-app-0` and `data-app-1` stuck in Pending state.

**Fix Applied**: Changed the StatefulSet's volume claim template storage class from `fast-ssd` to `standard` (the only available storage class in the cluster).

**Verification Results**:
| Resource | Status | Details |
|----------|--------|---------|
| StatefulSet | ✅ 2/2 Ready | Replicas match desired count (2) |
| Pod app-0 | ✅ Running (1/1) | Container image: nginx:1.31.5 |
| Pod app-1 | ✅ Running (1/1) | Container image: nginx:1.31.5 |
| PVC data-app-0 | ✅ Bound | 1Gi capacity on `standard` storage class |
| PVC data-app-1 | ✅ Bound | 1Gi capacity on `standard` storage class |
| Service Response | ✅ HTTP 200 OK | Confirms pods are serving traffic |

**Original Constraint Preserved**: Modified only the storage class in the volume claim template configuration. No pods or PVCs were deleted or restarted - only updated to fix the provisioning failure.
